question: A 28-year-old man comes to the physician for the evaluation of five episodes of painful oral ulcers over the past year. During this period, he has also had two painful genital ulcers that healed without treatment. He reports frequently having diffuse joint pain, malaise, and low-grade fever. There is no personal or family history of serious illness. He emigrated to the US from Syria with his family four years ago. He is sexually active with one female partner and they do not use condoms. He takes no medications. His temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), pulse is 90/min, and blood pressure is 130/80 mm Hg. Physical examination shows three painful ulcers on the oral buccal mucosa. Pelvic examination shows that the external genitalia has several healing scars. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Recurrent painful oral ulcers + genital ulcers -> Diffuse joint pain, malaise, low-grade fever -> No personal or family history of serious illness -> Emigrated from Syria -> Sexually active without condom use -> Healing scars on external genitalia -> Most likely diagnosis: Behcet disease -> 95%

CHAIN: Recurrent painful oral ulcers + genital ulcers -> Diffuse joint pain, malaise, low-grade fever -> No personal or family history of serious illness -> Emigrated from Syria -> Sexually active without condom use -> Healing scars on external genitalia -> Not consistent with Chancroid or Herpes simplex virus infection -> Most likely diagnosis: Behcet disease -> 85%
analysis: The patient's presentation with recurrent oral and genital ulcers, joint pain, and systemic symptoms is highly suggestive of Behcet's disease, which is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory disorder. Behcet's disease commonly affects young adults and is characterized by oral and genital ulcers, skin lesions, and eye involvement. The patient's history of emigrating from Syria, where Behcet's disease is more prevalent, also supports this diagnosis.
